# Hugh Carrow

## Overview

- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v1 c15 P37](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0037), [v2 c19 P50](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0050)</sub>
- **Origin:** Brierley  <sub>[v2 c19 P51](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0051), [v3 c20 P18](../source/v03-c20.md#nw-v03-c20-p0018), [v3 c20 P22](../source/v03-c20.md#nw-v03-c20-p0022)</sub>
- **Role:** Physician  <sub>[v4 c31 P12](../source/v04-c31.md#nw-v04-c31-p0012), [v4 c31 P15](../source/v04-c31.md#nw-v04-c31-p0015)</sub>
- **Titles:** Doctor  <sub>[v4 c31 P13](../source/v04-c31.md#nw-v04-c31-p0013), [v4 c31 P15](../source/v04-c31.md#nw-v04-c31-p0015)</sub>; President of the Freshman Class  <sub>[v3 c5 P0](../source/v03-c05.md#nw-v03-c05-p0000)</sub>

## Appearance

Hugh is a handsome, tall young man with broad shoulders, an open face, and bright, direct eyes. He strongly resembles his father, John Carrow, as a youth.

_Sources: [v1 c37 P38](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0038), [v2 c19 P50](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0050)_

## Personality

Hugh possesses a cheerful, practical nature and a keen sense of humor. He is brave enough to own up to his mistakes, straightforward in his expressions of affection, and maintains a high moral standard in his speech, thoughts, and actions.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P42](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0042), [v2 c19 P51](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0051), [v3 c27 P36](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0036)_

- handsome  <sub>[v1 c37 P38](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0038), [v2 c19 P50](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0050)</sub>
- good-humored  <sub>[v3 c27 P36](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0036), [v4 c15 P28](../source/v04-c15.md#nw-v04-c15-p0028)</sub>

## Goals

- to remain worthy of Nell Harcourt's companionship and love  <sub>[v2 c19 P51](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0051)</sub>
- to win Nell Harcourt's hand in marriage  <sub>[v3 c20 P31](../source/v03-c20.md#nw-v03-c20-p0031)</sub>

## History

As a boy at Brierley school, Hugh once teased Nell Harcourt by pulling her crimson braid and calling her "Carrots," causing her to break her slate over his head; despite taking the blame for the incident, he was temporarily met with her persistent refusal to forgive him. As he grew up, he developed a deep affection for Nell and strove to live a principled life worthy of her. During his college years at Wexcombe, he led the Freshmen to victory in the annual Arts Rush, was elected class president, and was initiated into the Lambs fraternity after undergoing a humorous public initiation in Portmaris. After one academic year, he offered Mayflowers to Nell and proposed to her, but she turned him down, asking that they remain only friends. He later worked for a newspaper and completed medical training at Portmaris Hospital, ultimately taking over Doctor Dave's medical practice at Seven Gulls Harbor. Eventually, he married Nell, settling with her near the harbor where they enjoyed summer excursions with friends and welcomed the truth regarding Laurence Vane's identity.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P33](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0033), [v1 c15 P38](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0038), [v1 c15 P42](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0042), [v1 c15 P47](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0047), [v2 c19 P51](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0051), [v3 c5 P0](../source/v03-c05.md#nw-v03-c05-p0000), [v3 c20 P31](../source/v03-c20.md#nw-v03-c20-p0031), [v3 c20 P34](../source/v03-c20.md#nw-v03-c20-p0034), [v3 c20 P39](../source/v03-c20.md#nw-v03-c20-p0039), [v3 c20 P23](../source/v03-c20.md#nw-v03-c20-p0023), [v4 c25 P0](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0000), [v4 c25 P14](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0014), [v4 c31 P12](../source/v04-c31.md#nw-v04-c31-p0012), [v4 c31 P15](../source/v04-c31.md#nw-v04-c31-p0015), [v4 c31 P19](../source/v04-c31.md#nw-v04-c31-p0019)_

## Quotes

> Mr. Pidgeon, the blame belongs to me because I provoked her.  <sub>[v1 c15 P42](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0042)</sub>

> Nell, I’m terribly apologetic about mocking your hair. Truly I am. Please don’t stay angry forever.  <sub>[v1 c15 P49](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0049)</sub>

> Nell, my love belongs to you. You are aware of that. I—I am unable to express the extent of it. Can you give me your word that you will marry me one day?  <sub>[v3 c20 P31](../source/v03-c20.md#nw-v03-c20-p0031)</sub>

> Comrades! Nell, I am unable to be fulfilled by your friendship. It is your love that I desire—yet you inform me that it will always be out of my reach.  <sub>[v3 c20 P41](../source/v03-c20.md#nw-v03-c20-p0041)</sub>
